# Job Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 420v–421r

---

**13:1** "Behold, all [this] my-eye has-seen [ra'atah], my-ear has-heard [shame'ah] and-understood [vatavin] it-for-itself.

**13:2** According-to-your-knowledge [keda'atkhem] I-also know [yadati]; not [am] I falling [nofel] from-you. **13:3** But-indeed [ulam] I to-Shaddai [the-Almighty] would-speak [adabber], and-to-argue [vehokheach] with God [el] I-desire [echpats].

**13:4** But-indeed [ve-ulam] you [are] plasterers of-lies [tofelei shaqer]; healers of-nothing [rofei elil] [are] all-of-you. **13:5** Would-that [mi yitten] being-silent you-would-be-silent [hacharesh tacharishun]; and-it-would-be to-you for-wisdom [le-chokhmah].

**13:6** Hear [shim'u] now my-argument [tochlachti], and-to-the-pleadings [verivot] of-my-lips give-attention [haqshivu]. **13:7** For-God [ha-le-el] will-you-speak wickedness [avlah]? And-for-him will-you-speak deceit [remiyah]? **13:8** His-face [panav] will-you-lift-up [tissa'un]? For-God will-you-contend [tarivun]?

**13:9** [Will it be] good [hatov] when he-searches-you-out [yachqor]? As-one-mocks [kahetel] a-man [be-enosh] will-you-mock [tahetelu] him? **13:10** He-will-surely-rebuke [hokheach yokhiach] you, if in-secret [basseter] you-lift-faces [tissa'un panim]. **13:11** Will-not his-exaltation [se'eto] terrify [tebaet] you, and-his-dread [pachdo] fall upon-you?

**13:12** Your-memorable-sayings [zikhronekhem] [are] proverbs of-ash [mishlei efer]; your-defenses [gabbkhem] [are] defenses of-clay [chomer].

**13:13** Be-silent [hacharishu] from-me and-I will-speak, and-let-pass [ya'avor] over me what-may. **13:14** Why [al mah] do-I-take [essa] my-flesh in-my-teeth, and-my-life [nafshi] I-put [asim] in-my-palm [bekapi]? **13:15** Behold, he-will-slay-me [yiqteleni] — I-have-no hope [lo ayachel] — but [akh] my-ways [derakhai] to-his-face [el panav] I-will-argue [okhiach].

**13:16** Also this to-me [is] salvation [lishuah], for a-godless-one [chanef] will-not come [yavo] before-his-face [lefanav]. **13:17** Hear [shim'u], hear [shamo'a] my-word [millati], and-my-declaration [achvati] [be] in-your-ears [be'oznekhem].

**13:18** Behold now, I-have-arranged [arakhti] [my] case [mishpat]; I-know that I am-righteous [etsdaq]. **13:19** Who [is] he [who] will-contend [yariv] with-me? For then I-would-be-silent [acharish] and-perish [ve-egva].

**13:20** Only two [things] do-not do [ta'as] to-me; then from-your-face [mippanekha] I-will-not hide [essater]. **13:21** Your-hand [kappekha] from-upon me put-far [harchaq], and-your-terror [eimatekha] let-it-not terrify-me [tevaateni].

**13:22** Then call [qera] and-I will-answer [e'eneh], or I-will-speak [adabber] and-you-reply [hashiveni]. **13:23** How-many [kammah] are-my-iniquities [avonot] and-sins [chattaot]? My-transgression [pish'i] and-my-sin [chattati] make-known [hodi'eni] to-me.

**13:24** Why [lammah] do-you-hide [tastir] your-face [panekha] and-count [tachsheveni] me as-your-enemy [le-oyev lakh]? **13:25** A-leaf [he'aleh] driven [niddaf] will-you-frighten [ta'arots]? And-dry stubble [qash yavesh] will-you-pursue [tirdof]?

**13:26** For you-write [tikhtov] bitter-things [merorot] against-me, and-you-make-me-inherit [vetorsheni] the-iniquities [avonot] of-my-youth [ne'urai]. **13:27** And-you-put [vetasem] in-the-stocks [bassad] my-feet [raglai], and-you-watch [vetishmor] all my-paths [orchotai]; upon the-roots [sharshei] of-my-feet you-set-a-mark [tithaqeh].

**13:28** And-he [is] like-a-rotten-thing [ke-raqav] that-wastes-away [yivleh], like-a-garment [keveged] that-a-moth [ash] has-eaten."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — tofelei shaqer:** Literally "plasterers of lies" — the image is of workmen smearing whitewash over a crumbling wall (cf. Ezekiel 13:10-16). The friends' theology is a cosmetic covering over falsehood.

**v.15 — The Kethiv/Qere problem:** The written text (*kethiv*) reads *lo* (לא, "not") — "I have no hope." The marginal reading (*qere*) is *lo* (לו, "to him") — "I will hope in him." This single letter creates two radically different readings: defiant despair or defiant faith. The EMET translation follows the kethiv.

**v.14 — "take my flesh in my teeth":** An idiom for risking everything, like an animal carrying prey in its jaws while fleeing. Job is staking his life on his case before God.

**v.27 — "upon the roots of my feet":** God marks the soles of Job's feet to track his every step — an image of surveillance that anticipates modern anxieties about divine oversight.

*— EMET*
